standfirst: Every figure on this site was produced by code in the repository, run against the corpus in the repository, on the date printed beside it. Nothing is quoted from a lecture slide, estimated, or rounded up. Where a result contradicted what I predicted, the prediction is still committed next to the result.
what_this_is: I built one evaluation harness, rag_eval.py (2,187 lines, four commands), and then spent thirteen sessions trying to break the pipeline it measures. The interesting results are mostly the negative ones. The guardrail I trusted most turned out to endorse the attack that beat it; the obvious fix for that attack catches none of it; and the library that promises durable execution loses a paid API call on its default setting.
shipping_note: Shipping configuration, unchanged since experiment 06 because nothing since has beaten it: bge-small · chunk 1000 · fixed · top-5 · rerank pool=20 · hardened prompt.
reference_intro: Thirteen pages compressing each topic to what is worth remembering. Written to be reread the night before an interview.
scope: This is applied LLM and RAG engineering, built on four years of Python, FastAPI, Docker and CI/CD backend work. It is not deep learning research, reinforcement learning, or MLOps at scale, and nothing here claims otherwise. One piece is deliberately unfinished and labelled as such: task 2 of experiment 04, the false positive hunt, was left blank rather than filled in after the fact.
